---
title: "Arming and Offboard Mode"
---

Before a ROS 2 node can send setpoints to PX4, the vehicle must be **armed**
and PX4 must be in **offboard mode**. Both transitions are triggered by
publishing `VehicleCommand` messages. The sequence has strict ordering
requirements and timing constraints.

---

## Required sequence

```
1. Start streaming OffboardControlMode heartbeat  (>=2 Hz, before switching)
2. Start streaming setpoints                       (same rate as control loop)
3. Send VehicleCommand: VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE -> OFFBOARD
4. Send VehicleCommand: VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM -> ARM
```

Steps 1–2 must begin **before** step 3. PX4 rejects the offboard mode switch
if it has not already seen a recent `OffboardControlMode` message. Keep both
streams running continuously thereafter.

---

## VehicleCommand helper

```cpp
/* vehicle_command.hpp */
#pragma once
#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>
#include <px4_msgs/msg/vehicle_command.hpp>

inline void send_vehicle_command(
    rclcpp::Publisher<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleCommand>::SharedPtr& pub,
    rclcpp::Node* node,
    uint32_t command,
    float param1 = 0.0f,
    float param2 = 0.0f)
{
    px4_msgs::msg::VehicleCommand msg{};
    msg.timestamp       = node->get_clock()->now().nanoseconds() / 1000;
    msg.command         = command;
    msg.param1          = param1;
    msg.param2          = param2;
    msg.target_system   = 1;
    msg.target_component = 1;
    msg.source_system   = 1;
    msg.source_component = 1;
    msg.from_external   = true;
    pub->publish(msg);
}
```

---

## Switching to offboard mode

```cpp
#include <px4_msgs/msg/vehicle_command.hpp>

/* PX4_CUSTOM_MAIN_MODE_OFFBOARD = 6 */
send_vehicle_command(
    vehicle_cmd_pub_, this,
    px4_msgs::msg::VehicleCommand::VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE,
    1.0f,   // base mode: custom
    6.0f);  // custom main mode: offboard
```

PX4 switches only if it has received `OffboardControlMode` messages recently.
If the switch fails, `VehicleStatus.nav_state` stays at its prior value.

---

## Arming

```cpp
send_vehicle_command(
    vehicle_cmd_pub_, this,
    px4_msgs::msg::VehicleCommand::VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM,
    1.0f);  // 1.0 = arm, 0.0 = disarm
```

---

## Disarming

```cpp
send_vehicle_command(
    vehicle_cmd_pub_, this,
    px4_msgs::msg::VehicleCommand::VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM,
    0.0f);  // disarm
```

---

## Monitoring vehicle state

Subscribe to `VehicleStatus` to read the current arming and nav state:

```cpp
#include <px4_msgs/msg/vehicle_status.hpp>

auto qos = rclcpp::QoS(10).best_effort();

status_sub_ = create_subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus>(
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1", qos,
    [this](const px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus::SharedPtr msg) {
        armed_       = (msg->arming_state ==
                        px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus::ARMING_STATE_ARMED);
        in_offboard_ = (msg->nav_state ==
                        px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus::NAVIGATION_STATE_OFFBOARD);
    });
```

::: {.callout-note}
The topic is `/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1` (versioned) from PX4 v1.14 onward.
See [Versioned topic names](../setup/workspace-setup.qmd#versioned-topic-names).
:::

Relevant `VehicleStatus` constants:

| Field | Constant | Value |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `arming_state` | `ARMING_STATE_DISARMED` | 1 |
| `arming_state` | `ARMING_STATE_ARMED` | 2 |
| `nav_state` | `NAVIGATION_STATE_OFFBOARD` | 14 |

---

## Full arming state machine

A typical controller node follows this pattern on startup:

```cpp
/* Called at ~10 Hz in the main control timer */
void control_loop()
{
    /* 1. Always publish heartbeat first */
    publish_offboard_control_mode();

    /* 2. Always publish a setpoint (zeros are fine pre-arm) */
    publish_setpoint();

    /* 3. After a short warm-up, switch mode and arm */
    if (!mode_sent_ && ++tick_ > 10) {   // ~1 s at 10 Hz
        switch_to_offboard();
        arm();
        mode_sent_ = true;
    }
}
```

The tick counter gives PX4 time to receive a few heartbeats before the mode
switch is requested.

---

## Production FSM pattern

The tick-counter approach above has two weaknesses: it fires the commands once
and never retries, and it has no way to detect a mode flip or disarm after
arming. A production controller should use a proper state machine.

**State sequence:**

```
WAITING_FOR_ODOM
  -> on first odometry:            PUBLISHING_OFFBOARD  (record t0)
PUBLISHING_OFFBOARD
  -> after preamble (e.g. 2 s):   emit SetOffboardMode, REQUESTING_OFFBOARD
REQUESTING_OFFBOARD
  -> nav_state == OFFBOARD:        emit ArmDisarm, REQUESTING_ARM
  -> every retry_s:                re-emit SetOffboardMode
REQUESTING_ARM
  -> arming_state == ARMED:        ARMED
  -> every retry_s:                re-emit ArmDisarm
ARMED
  -> terminal
```

**Why wait for odometry before publishing?** PX4 will not enter offboard mode
if it has not yet received a valid state estimate. Gating on first odometry
receipt ensures EKF2 is up before the preamble starts.

**Implementation** — keep the FSM ROS-free so it can be unit-tested without
spinning a node. The node feeds it raw status fields; the FSM returns an action
tag:

```cpp
/* offboard_arm_fsm.hpp — no rclcpp or px4_msgs includes */
enum class ArmState {
  WAITING_FOR_ODOM,
  PUBLISHING_OFFBOARD,
  REQUESTING_OFFBOARD,
  REQUESTING_ARM,
  ARMED,
};

enum class FsmAction { None, SetOffboardMode, ArmDisarm };

class OffboardArmFsm {
 public:
  static constexpr uint8_t kNavStateOffboard  = 14;
  static constexpr uint8_t kArmingStateArmed  = 2;

  explicit OffboardArmFsm(double preamble_s = 2.0, double retry_s = 1.0)
      : preamble_s_(preamble_s), retry_s_(retry_s) {}

  FsmAction step(bool odom_received, uint8_t nav_state,
                 uint8_t arming_state, double now_s) {
    switch (state_) {
      case ArmState::WAITING_FOR_ODOM:
        if (odom_received) { state_ = ArmState::PUBLISHING_OFFBOARD;
                             t0_ = now_s; }
        return FsmAction::None;

      case ArmState::PUBLISHING_OFFBOARD:
        if (now_s - t0_ >= preamble_s_) {
          state_ = ArmState::REQUESTING_OFFBOARD;
          last_req_ = now_s;
          return FsmAction::SetOffboardMode;
        }
        return FsmAction::None;

      case ArmState::REQUESTING_OFFBOARD:
        if (nav_state == kNavStateOffboard) {
          state_ = ArmState::REQUESTING_ARM;
          last_req_ = now_s;
          return FsmAction::ArmDisarm;
        }
        if (now_s - last_req_ >= retry_s_) { last_req_ = now_s;
                                              return FsmAction::SetOffboardMode; }
        return FsmAction::None;

      case ArmState::REQUESTING_ARM:
        if (arming_state == kArmingStateArmed) {
          state_ = ArmState::ARMED; return FsmAction::None;
        }
        if (now_s - last_req_ >= retry_s_) { last_req_ = now_s;
                                              return FsmAction::ArmDisarm; }
        return FsmAction::None;

      case ArmState::ARMED:
        return FsmAction::None;
    }
    return FsmAction::None;
  }

  /* Use this as the gate for publishing actuator setpoints.
   * Checks FSM state AND live status — a disarm or mode flip
   * immediately closes the gate even if FSM is in ARMED. */
  bool armedAndOffboard(uint8_t nav_state, uint8_t arming_state) const {
    return state_ == ArmState::ARMED &&
           nav_state    == kNavStateOffboard &&
           arming_state == kArmingStateArmed;
  }

 private:
  double preamble_s_, retry_s_;
  ArmState state_ = ArmState::WAITING_FOR_ODOM;
  double t0_ = 0.0, last_req_ = 0.0;
};
```

**Node integration:**

```cpp
// In the control timer callback:
const double now_s = this->now().nanoseconds() * 1e-9;
const auto action = fsm_.step(odom_received_, nav_state_, arming_state_, now_s);

switch (action) {
  case FsmAction::SetOffboardMode:
    send_vehicle_command(cmd_pub_, this,
        VehicleCommand::VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE, 1.0f, 6.0f);
    break;
  case FsmAction::ArmDisarm:
    send_vehicle_command(cmd_pub_, this,
        VehicleCommand::VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM, 1.0f, 21196.0f);
    break;
  case FsmAction::None: break;
}

// Gate actuator output on the dual check:
if (fsm_.armedAndOffboard(nav_state_, arming_state_)) {
    publish_actuator_setpoints();
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
`param2 = 21196.0f` in the arm command is the force-arm magic number required
when arming from a companion computer (bypasses some safety checks that require
a physical RC switch). Use `0.0f` if you want the standard safety checks.
:::

**Warm-start observers on arm transition** — run state estimators or observers
open-loop while waiting for arm so they have converged state by the time the
vehicle lifts off. Reset integrators from the current measurement on the first
armed tick to avoid windup:

```cpp
if (fsm_.armedAndOffboard(nav_state_, arming_state_) && !was_armed_) {
    reset_observers_from_current_state();
    was_armed_ = true;
}
```

**Why keep the FSM ROS-free?** The class only takes primitive types
(`uint8_t`, `double`, `bool`). You can instantiate it in a plain GTest fixture
with no `rclcpp::init` and drive it with synthetic status values — full branch
coverage without a running ROS graph.

---

## Takeoff after arming

After arming, the vehicle is on the ground with motors spinning at idle. Command
a TrajectorySetpoint with a target altitude to begin the takeoff:

```cpp
px4_msgs::msg::TrajectorySetpoint traj{};
traj.timestamp = get_clock()->now().nanoseconds() / 1000;

/* NED frame: negative z = above ground */
traj.position  = {0.0f, 0.0f, -2.0f};  // 2 m above ground
traj.yaw       = 0.0f;                  // North-facing
traj_pub_->publish(traj);
```

Use `OffboardControlMode` with `position = true` while climbing:

```cpp
mode_msg.position = true;
mode_msg.velocity = false;
mode_msg.attitude = false;
```

Switch `OffboardControlMode` fields to match whichever control mode you
activate once at altitude. See
[Low-Level Offboard Control](low-level-control.qmd).

---

## Safety: continuous stream requirement

PX4 exits offboard mode if the `OffboardControlMode` stream stops for more than
~500 ms. It also disarms if the vehicle is commanded with zero throttle while
on the ground in offboard mode for more than ~1 s.

Keep two independent timers:

```cpp
// Heartbeat: 10 Hz is safe margin above the 2 Hz minimum
offboard_timer_ = create_wall_timer(100ms, [this]() {
    publish_offboard_control_mode();
});

// Control output: 100 Hz
control_timer_ = create_wall_timer(10ms, [this]() {
    publish_setpoint();
});
```

The timers are independent so a slow control computation does not starve the
heartbeat.

---

## Troubleshooting

### Vehicle never arms

1. Check pre-arm checks: `ros2 topic echo /fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1 | grep arming`.
2. In SITL, the EKF2 estimator must be healthy before arming. Wait ~5 s after
   SITL starts.
3. Ensure `OffboardControlMode` is being published before sending the arm
   command — PX4 refuses to arm for offboard if no heartbeat has arrived.

### Offboard mode switch is accepted but vehicle falls

The `OffboardControlMode` was set with `position = true` but no
`TrajectorySetpoint` is being published. The position controller has no target
and commands zero thrust. Always publish a setpoint at the current position
immediately after arming.

### Vehicle disarms immediately after takeoff

The motor output stream (`ActuatorMotors`) stopped. PX4 exits offboard mode and
auto-disarms. Check that your control timer is running without exceptions.
